title: 1892 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship
text:
{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox Hurling All-Ireland | year = 1892 | image = | dates = 30 October 1892 – 26 March 1893 | teams = 3 | connacht = | munster = Cork | leinster = Dublin | ulster = | matches = 2 | poty = | team = Cork | titles = 2nd | captain = [[Bill O'Callaghan]] | manager = | team2 = Dublin | captain2 = Pat Egan | manager2 = | totalgoals = 10 (5.00 per game) | totalpoints = 16 (8.00 per game) | topscorer = | previous = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1891|1891]] | next = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1893|1893]] }} The '''1892 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the sixth staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s premier [[inter-county]] [[hurling]] tournament. The championship ran from 30 October 1892 to 26 March 1893. [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]] were the [[1891 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|defending champions]], however, they were beaten by [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the [[#Munster final|Munster final]].{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport-columnists/arid-20455875.html|title=A hurling enclave that has stood the test of time|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=28 July 2017|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}}{{cite news|url=https://www.terracetalk.com/articles/GAA/486/The-1891-Hurling-Final--The-Aftermath|title=The 1891 Hurling Final - The Aftermath|publisher=Terrace Talk|date=29 May 2014|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}}{{cite news|url=https://www.gaa.ie/article/history-woven-into-the-colours-sported-in-battle|title=History woven into the colours sported in battle|publisher=GAA website|date=23 July 2026|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}} The [[#All-Ireland final|All-Ireland final]] was played on 26 March 1893 at [[Clonturk Park]] in [[Dublin]], between Cork and [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]], in what was their first ever meeting in the All-Ireland final.{{cite news|url=https://hoganstand.com/county/cork/article/index/198271|title=Cork and Dublin bridge 85-year gap|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=7 August 2013|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}}{{cite news|url=https://www.dublingaa.ie/news/recent-meetings-dublin-v-cork-hurling|title=Recent meetings: Dublin v Cork (hurling)|publisher=Dublin GAA website|date=29 July 2021|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}} Cork won the match by 2–03 to 1–05 to become the first team to win a second title.{{cite news|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-40163136.html|title=We had to bring on a 61-year-old to make up the numbers... Redmonds chairman explains why one of Cork's oldest clubs is going out of existence|publisher=Echo Live|date=20 September 2018|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}}{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-30870483.html|title=Historic Cork club Redmonds set to shut its doors|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=21 September 2018|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}}{{cite news|url=https://hoganstand.com/County/UK/Article/Index/290575|title=Famous Cork GAA club to disband|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=21 September 2018|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}} ==Rule changes== At the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s (GAA) annual congress held in [[Thurles]] on 13 January 1892, some changes were made to the existing rules of the game. Firstly, a goal was made equal to five points. Secondly, teams were reduced from twenty-one to seventeen players. Perhaps most importantly of all, it was also decided that county champions, when representing the county, were allowed to select players from other clubs within the county.{{citation | url = https://doras.dcu.ie/18960/3/J_F_Lennon_V3.pdf | via = doras.dcu.ie | title = Towards a philosophy for legislation in Gaelic games, Appendix 2 | first = Joseph F. | last = Lennon | publisher = Northern Recreation Consultants | date = 1999 | oclc = 795763417 | page = 645 }} ==Participating teams== {| class="wikitable" |- !rowspan="2"|County !rowspan="2"|Club !colspan="2"|Most recent success !rowspan="2"| |- !All-Ireland !Provincial |- |[[Cork GAA|Cork]] |[[Redmonds GAA|Redmonds]] |[[1890 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1890]] |[[1890 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1890]] |{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/Cork/ClubTitles|title=Club Titles - Cork|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=|access-date=30 July 2026}} |- |[[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] |[[Faughs GAA|Davitt–Faughs]] |[[1889 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1889]] |[[1889 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|1889]] |{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/Dublin/ClubTitles|title=Club Titles - Dublin|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=|access-date=30 July 2026}} |- |[[Kerry GAA|Kerry]] |[[Kilmoyley GAA|Kilmoyley]] |[[1891 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1891]] |[[1891 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1891]] |{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/Kerry/ClubTitles|title=Club Titles - Kerry|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=|access-date=30 July 2026}} |} ==[[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]]== ===Munster final=== {{football box collapsible | date = 30 October 1892 | round = Final | team1 = [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]]

{{small|[[Faughs GAA|(Davitt–Faughs)]]}} | goals1 = | goals2 = | stadium = [[Clonturk Park]] | attendance = 5,000 | referee = D Fraher (Waterford) }} ==Championship statistics== ===Miscellaneous=== * The All-Ireland final ended in disarray when the [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] players walked off with five minutes left in the match following a dispute over a goal.{{cite news|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corknews/arid-41668541.html|title=Nostalgia: Cork hurling remains a constant in a changing world|publisher=Echo Live|date=13 July 2025|accessdate=30 July 2026|first=|last=}} ==Sources== * Corry, Eoghan, ''The GAA Book of Lists'' (Hodder Headline Ireland, 2005). * Donegan, Des, ''The Complete Handbook of Gaelic Games'' (DBA Publications Limited, 2005). ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Hurling All-Irelands}} [[Category:All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championships|1892]] [[Category:1892 in Irish sport]]
